bygone

BY-gon -- from 'by' + 'gone'; almost always used in the phrase 'a bygone era.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Bygone is belonging to an earlier time now past, usually with a nostalgic or wistful tone.

The old soda fountain feels like a cheerful relic of some bygone era.

Example

The restored train station, with its brass fixtures and hand-painted signs, felt like a little piece of a bygone era.

Notice the warm, wistful tone -- nobody's mocking the train station the way antediluvian would. Bygone simply admires something from an earlier time that's now gone, gently and fondly.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

olden: Olden survives almost only in the phrase 'the olden days,' a cozy, storybook way of pointing at long ago. Bygone is its more grown-up cousin: just as warm and nostalgic, but at home in ordinary writing about a bygone era or bygone days.

past: Past is the plainest word for time gone by -- the past decade, past mistakes -- and it carries no feeling at all. Bygone adds the sigh: a bygone era is not just earlier, it is fondly missed.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

current: happening or existing right now

upcoming: going to happen in the near future

Where it sits · how completely lost to the past

former → bygone → vanished

former vs. bygone: Former is milder than bygone: a former mill still stands there under a new name, barely lost at all, while bygone mourns an era that has slipped entirely out of reach.

vanished vs. bygone: Vanished is stronger than bygone: a bygone era still lives on in memory and old photographs, but a vanished streetcar line has been wiped away so completely that hardly a trace survives.

Build the Word

The pieces

particle — by-: past, aside (English)

root — -gone-: past form of 'go' (English)

Put it together: Bygone simply combines 'by' (past, aside) with 'gone' -- the plainest possible way of saying something has passed -- which is why 'a bygone era' has such a gentle, nostalgic ring to it: it's just describing time that has quietly slipped by.

Use the root in a new word: undergone: Police asked every bystander for a name and a phone number.

Root Check

Word Choice

Bygone is almost always paired with 'era' or 'days' ('a bygone era,' 'in bygone days') and carries a fond, nostalgic tone. Compare "antediluvian," which mocks something as absurdly outdated, and "antecedent," which isn't about nostalgia at all but about a logical cause-and-effect relationship.
